title: A spectrum through gas
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: When light passes through suitable cooler gas, atoms can absorb particular wavelengths. Those wavelengths appear as dark lines in a continuous spectrum.

misconception: A learner may choose: A telescope removing every wavelength equally
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: What can produce dark absorption lines in an otherwise continuous spectrum?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: What can produce dark absorption lines in an otherwise continuous spectrum? Cooler gas absorbing specific wavelengths. When light passes through suitable cooler gas, atoms can absorb particular wavelengths. Those wavelengths appear as dark lines in a continuous spectrum.
Visual caption: Gas removes specific light. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: What can produce dark absorption lines in an otherwise continuous spectrum?
options: A telescope removing every wavelength equally
The absence of atoms anywhere along the light path
